extracted.intended_audience: USPTO personnel (patent examiners) and patent practitioners/applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for evaluating whether patent claims are directed to statutory subject matter under 35 U.S.C. 101, including USPTO memoranda, example claim analyses, quick reference sheets, and incorporation into the MPEP. The page is an archival index of eligibility guidance by date of issuance and associated materials (examples, charts, memos).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance explaining how USPTO personnel, including patent examiners, should evaluate claims for patent subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current guidance is found in the MPEP Sections 2103 through 2106.07(c). The page is an archival listing of documents that have governed eligibility analyses over time and points examiners/practitioners to the controlling MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the MPEP (Sections 2103–2106.07(c)) as controlling guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office's current eligibility guidance is found in the Manual of Patent Examination Procedure (MPEP) Sections 2103 through 2106.07(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents issued prior to incorporation into the MPEP may have been superseded; examiners should follow the MPEP provisions as the operative procedure for eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: October 2019 Patent Eligibility Guidance Update
rubrics_metrics.description: The October 2019 update (issued October 17, 2019) providing updated patent eligibility guidance and associated materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Appendix 1 (October 2019 Examples 43–46), Appendix 2 (Index of Examples), and Appendix 3 (Chart of Subject Matter Eligibility Court Decisions). These materials were incorporated into the Ninth Edition, Revision 10.2019 of the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance (January 7, 2019)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised guidance issued January 7, 2019 addressing patent eligibility and discussing how the 2019 PEG affected the former version of the MPEP (Ninth Edition Revision 08.2017).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an updated framework for examiners and was incorporated into the MPEP; used to clarify examination practice following intervening case law and public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2014 Interim Eligibility Guidance (2014 IEG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance (Federal Register notice December 2014) to assist USPTO personnel when determining subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101 in view of Supreme Court decisions (Alice, Myriad, Mayo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2014 IEG supplements earlier preliminary examination instructions, and it superseded the March 4, 2014 Procedure for Subject Matter Eligibility Analysis of Claims Reciting or Involving Laws of Nature/Natural Principles, Natural Phenomena, and/or Natural Products. It includes a quick reference sheet and example sets (nature-based product examples, abstract idea examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: July 2015 Update on Subject Matter Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Update (July 30, 2015) that incorporates public comments on the 2014 IEG and provides additional examiner guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes appendix of examples, an index of eligibility examples, a compilation of subject matter eligibility court decisions, and an interim eligibility guidance quick reference sheet to assist examiners applying the 2014 IEG.

rubrics_metrics.name: May 2016 Subject Matter Eligibility Update (best practices memorandum)
rubrics_metrics.description: May 2016 memorandum and Federal Register notice providing guidance, including best practices for formulating a subject matter eligibility rejection and evaluating the applicant’s response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains subject matter eligibility examples (life sciences), an index of examples, and an updated list of subject matter eligibility court decisions. Advises examiners on how to compose rejections and how to consider applicant responses in light of eligibility jurisprudence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoranda addressing Federal Circuit and other court decisions (e.g., Berkheimer, Vanda, Finjan, Core Wireless, Enfish, McRO, BASCOM, Rapid Litigation Management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Series of memoranda discussing how particular court decisions affect subject matter eligibility analysis and examiner procedures (issued various dates in 2016–2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include 'Revising 101 Eligibility Procedure in view of Berkheimer v. HP, Inc.' (April 19, 2018) and memoranda summarizing recent decisions (Vanda, Finjan, Core Wireless). These memoranda provide targeted instructions to examiners on applying case law to exam practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Quick Reference Sheets (including 'Identifying Abstract Ideas' and interim quick reference sheets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise reference materials intended to help examiners identify abstract ideas and apply eligibility guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes that all versions of the Office's 'Eligibility Quick Reference Sheet Identifying Abstract Ideas' (first issued July 2015, updated July 2018) have been superseded by subsequent guidance. Other quick reference sheets (e.g., December 2016 Interim Eligibility Quick Reference Sheet) accompanied updates and example sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligibility examples (nature-based, abstract idea, life sciences, business methods, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets of hypothetical and claim-based examples illustrating how to perform subject matter eligibility analyses across technologies (e.g., nature-based product examples, abstract idea examples, life sciences examples, business method examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provide exemplary subject matter eligibility analyses of hypothetical claims and claims drawn from case law to guide examiners on applying the eligibility framework in specific fact patterns (e.g., December 2016 business method examples; May 2016 life sciences examples; July 2015 and October 2019 example appendices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and charts of subject matter eligibility court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Charts and indices compiling court decisions relevant to subject matter eligibility, updated periodically (e.g., Appendix 3, 'Chart of Subject Matter Eligibility Court Decisions').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a reference to see how courts have decided eligibility issues and to inform examiner application of precedent; updates accompany guidance releases (e.g., July 2015 appendix, December 2016 update, October 2019 chart).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions holding claims eligible (quick reference sheet updated July 23, 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quick reference sheet listing decisions in which claims were held eligible, intended as a quick guide for examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples and citations of cases where courts found claims to be eligible; included among materials to inform examiner practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction not to rely on superseded guidance (procedural constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance issued prior to the Ninth Edition, Revision 10.2019 of the MPEP (revised June 2020) should not be relied upon; earlier guidance has been incorporated into the MPEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The archival page explicitly warns examiners/practitioners that eligibility-related guidance issued prior to the Ninth Edition, Revision 10.2019 should not be relied upon and that many earlier quick reference materials have been superseded by subsequent guidance incorporated into the MPEP.
